claims.claim: Reviewers describe crashing issues when attempting to play in VR mode.

citations.review_text: Constantly crashing on my every attempt to play it on VR.

Absolutely unmatched aircraft systems simulation, cockpit interactivity, flight models and graphics. If you are a nerd and want to fly combat aircraft, read manuals, learn systems and shoot targets - this is as good as it gets.  

If you're looking for a combat simulator - yeah, this is not it, despite the name. Enemy AI is simply terrible. You have to go to multiplayer if you want challenging and fair Air-to-Air battles and some semblance of your actions mattering.

It also has atrocious VR performance, insane disk space requirements, and many many other ridiculous technical issues. If you want to play this in VR - you need literally the best PC money can buy, and even then be ready to make some sacrifices. 

Keep in mind that despite the store page not mentioning this, this game is not playable with a mouse and keyboard. A flight stick, or at least an xbox/ps controller are REQUIRED to play.

Don't play the Steam version, get it on their website. You get free trials for most aircraft in the game.

Works on Linux with tweaks, but includes a launcher that doesn't. You'll need to edit config files to disable the launcher. I do not recommend it though, dual booting into Windows is worth it to not lose CPU performance with DXVK.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that configuring controls and keybinds for different aircraft takes a significant amount of time and specialized hardware like a flight stick or HOTAS.

citations.review_text:
I enjoy French planes and can fly the Mirage F1, so I'm happy with it!

I like making custom missions with flight paths with nice scenery, using custom liveries and flying community campains too.

The learning curve was steep but it's part of the fun for me: learning the different aircraft systems and configuring Joystick, Throttle, or XBox Controller and coming up with the ideal control scheme for my playstyle.

I'd be happy to play it with my friends, like in the Mirage F1B, as example, but it's already pretty fun in solo!

Go for it if you see an aircraft which you like.

I made some purchases for this game during the summer sale, and so far I'm happy with my purchases.  The base game is free, but if you don't want to spend a lot, get the flaming cliffs expansion.  You get some good planes that are not fully interactive like the more expensive models, but they fly well and the startup procedures are less complicated.  You can pvp with them and they're quite fun.  If you want to play a realistic combat flight sim, this is very enjoyable.  So far, I have completed the training missions for the F-14, and the SU-27.  Each aircraft has a different set of keybinds,  I'm using my pair of VKB Gladiators NXT Evo,  and if you have flight sticks or HOTAS, it is time consuming to configure for each aircraft.  However, I just configure mine as I go through the flight training for each aircraft.  I have figured out how to save settings and load them to another profile and it's helpful with the different variants of the same flight model like the Su-27, Su-33, and J-11.

Very fun game but you need a lot of equipment to truly enjoy it, such as a VR headset or head tracking, as well as a stick and throttle. The modules and DLCs you can buy are pretty overpriced, but they definitely include a lot of fun stuff.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the learning curve as extremely steep and challenging, requiring considerable patience and time to master aircraft systems.

citations.review_text:
I enjoy French planes and can fly the Mirage F1, so I'm happy with it!

I like making custom missions with flight paths with nice scenery, using custom liveries and flying community campains too.

The learning curve was steep but it's part of the fun for me: learning the different aircraft systems and configuring Joystick, Throttle, or XBox Controller and coming up with the ideal control scheme for my playstyle.

I'd be happy to play it with my friends, like in the Mirage F1B, as example, but it's already pretty fun in solo!

Go for it if you see an aircraft which you like.

DCS World is one of those rare games that I genuinely love, even though I have a few complaints.

The level of detail in the aircraft is incredible. Every switch, system, and weapon feels like it was built with care, and that's what makes DCS stand out from every other combat flight simulator. I also love the flight models, the aircraft mechanics, and the steep learning curve. Learning to fly and operate a new aircraft is challenging, but that's exactly what makes it so rewarding.

The modding community is another huge positive. There are some amazing mods that add even more variety to the game. Even playing on my admittedly not-so-great laptop in VR, I've had an incredible experience.

My biggest complaint is how difficult it is for new players who don't have the money to buy additional modules. Without using mods, you're essentially limited to the free aircraft unless you're willing to spend around $80 on a full-fidelity module. While mods are a great part of the DCS community, many of the most popular ones require paid modules to function. For example, the F-22 mod requires the F-15C, and the Su-30SM mod requires both the free Su-25 and the paid Su-33. That means even free mods can still have a financial barrier.

I'd love to see Eagle Dynamics introduce a progression system where players could unlock a few aircraft through gameplay. Maybe players could earn a basic jet fighter, an attack helicopter, and a propeller aircraft by completing a series of increasingly difficult missions. Then, after finishing an even more demanding set of challenges, they could unlock one full-fidelity aircraft, such as the F-16C, F/A-18C, or A-10C II. I think that would make DCS much more approachable for new players while still preserving the value of paid modules.

My last complaint is a simple one: where's the Su-30SM? I'd buy that module the day it released.

Even with those complaints, DCS World remains one of the best combat flight simulators available. If you're wi…

If you’re looking for true realism, DCS is hands down the best flight simulator on the market. Yes, the learning curve is incredibly steep and getting into the high-fidelity modules can be an expensive hobby, but nothing else even comes close to the feeling of flipping actual cockpit switches and finally mastering a complex fighter jet. It requires a lot of patience, but the payoff and sense of immersion are completely unmatched

If you play this game expecting to get a good experience off the base modules, or flying with an XBOX controller, then you are ultimately going to be disappointed in the experience you get. But, if you go in ready to buy a couple modules and get yourself a decent HOTAS, then you will have a great time.

Became my go-to game after a while of exploring and getting tired of most fan-favourite 3A titles
I've never touched onto flight sims before and therefore tried out MSFS and DCS
MSFS was great, for an airliner, where I flew with a basic joystick across the globe and visited my house irl... it's a great game and only game that does it well out there. However aside from that, all the planes are just a little dull and too sim-like. I wanted something with greater detail, better immersion, something fun.
I loved the f/a-18 super hornet in MSFS so I watched a few yt vids and found DCS.

Oh boy do I regret it. I've since spent around 600 bucks, on 2 better joysticks, 6 planes, a map and still going strong. I've heard from people who have spent 2000 on a single vr and built a whole cockpit. And man am I amazed.
Within the first hundred hours, I learned two planes. Not even into detail but only the controls, flight dynamics and surface-level systems. There is NO game that's taken me over 50 hours to complete, so far. This one's different. You'd have to remember things, jot down notes and pray that you don't forget how to fly the last plane you just learned. Flying the f18, sure, was easy once I got the hang of how the systems work, why they are set up that way, all the controls and necessary info from around a dozen tutorials and sometimes text guides. But the sheer possibilities still amaze me. Every day I can learn something new, from the forums. I can't stress about the fact that all full-fidelity modules are almost if not all FULLY FUNCTIONAL and a 1:1 to real-life. It's almost corny to say that but this is the only game that fully simulates it, perhaps apart from BMS which only really focused on the f16. All the weapons, air to ground, air to air... have different operating modes like ccip ccrp, tracking...
You can learn history from this game, which I've briefly touched upon but the countless planes each have so much depth to them it takes over the time of finishing a…

The good: very detailed combat flight sim. If you like flying then you can easily spend hundreds of hours here.

The bad: While the core is free the modules cost. Each individual one. There are some free 3rd party mods out there but usually lack in polish or function. Still worth checking out. Usually need a paid mod in order to work.

The real bad: Outdated training. Good luck trying to learn with the in house training. You're better off searching google/youtube for how to's. Since each individual mod requires to be paid for there should really be much better and updated training missions/campaigns.

Still a lot of fun, but be prepared for hours of frustration first.

คนส่วนใหญ่จะเลิกเล่นเพราะไม่เข้าใจระบบเกมนี้ มันคือระบบเครื่องบินที่สมจริงที่สุดเท่าที่เคยเล่ยเกม Flight SIM
นี่คือสุดยอดเกมที่ทำให้ความฝันของผมเป็นจริง ผมชอบการบินมาก ยิ่งสมจริง ยิ่งชอบ (สำหรับผม) มันไม่ใช่แค่เพียงคุณจะเล่นได้ แต่เกมนี้ มันบังคับให้คุณต้องศึกษาระบบของเครื่องบินอย่างจริงจัง ถ้าอยากจะสนุกกับมัน และคุณจะได้ความรู้ของระบบเครื่องบินแต่ละรุ่นด้วย ถึงจะไม่ใช่นักบินจริงๆ แต่ว่าคุณก็คือนักบินในเกม

*******
I was genuinely worried about reviewing this game.

I invested a significant amount of money in flight simulation equipment just to experience it the way it was meant to be played. In the end, I still chose to recommend it.

This is **not** a game you can fully understand in just three hours. You need to study how each aircraft actually works—from the A-10, F-16, and F-15 to the B-3 (or any other aircraft you choose to fly). Every aircraft has its own systems, procedures, and flight characteristics.

Most people give up because they don't understand the game's systems. This is the most realistic flight simulation I've ever played.

This game made one of my biggest dreams come true. I've always loved aviation, and the more realistic a simulator is, the more I enjoy it.

For me, this isn't just a game that lets you fly. It **forces** you to seriously learn how each aircraft operates if you truly want to enjoy the experience. Along the way, you'll gain real knowledge about aircraft systems as well.

You may not be a pilot in real life, but when you're in this game, you truly become one.

Became my go-to game after a while of exploring and getting tired of most fan-favourite 3A titles
I've never touched onto flight sims before and therefore tried out MSFS and DCS
MSFS was great, for an airliner, where I flew with a basic joystick across the globe and visited my house irl... it's a great game and only game that does it well out there. However aside from that, all the planes are just a little dull and too sim-like. I wanted something with greater detail, better immersion, something fun.
I loved the f/a-18 super hornet in MSFS so I watched a few yt vids and found DCS.

Oh boy do I regret it. I've since spent around 600 bucks, on 2 better joysticks, 6 planes, a map and still going strong. I've heard from people who have spent 2000 on a single vr and built a whole cockpit. And man am I amazed.
Within the first hundred hours, I learned two planes. Not even into detail but only the controls, flight dynamics and surface-level systems. There is NO game that's taken me over 50 hours to complete, so far. This one's different. You'd have to remember things, jot down notes and pray that you don't forget how to fly the last plane you just learned. Flying the f18, sure, was easy once I got the hang of how the systems work, why they are set up that way, all the controls and necessary info from around a dozen tutorials and sometimes text guides. But the sheer possibilities still amaze me. Every day I can learn something new, from the forums. I can't stress about the fact that all full-fidelity modules are almost if not all FULLY FUNCTIONAL and a 1:1 to real-life. It's almost corny to say that but this is the only game that fully simulates it, perhaps apart from BMS which only really focused on the f16. All the weapons, air to ground, air to air... have different operating modes like ccip ccrp, tracking...
You can learn history from this game, which I've briefly touched upon but the countless planes each have so much depth to them it takes over the time of finishing a…

Played this game for almost 3 years now, very much recommend. If you're looking for the most realistic combat flight sim out there, this is it. It has many full fidelity favorites from different eras such as A-10, F-16C, F-14, F-18C, F-4E, AJS-37, MiG-15, MiG-21, MiG-29, Mirage F1, and a variety of helicopters(though mainly $60-80), and lower fidelity modules like the Su-27/33, MiG-29, F-15C (FC2024 bundle). I recommend buying on sales, which happen somewhat often, usually 30-50% off. Additionally, there are many free mods for this game that are very high quality, like F-22, Su-30, Su-35, and A-4. (Su-30/35 and A-4 are standalone, meaning you can fly them for free.) 

I started with just keyboard and mouse, but I highly, highly recommend using a joystick for this game. It has a very steep learning curve. Don't spend an hour downloading and expect to be in the air in 10 minutes, and kicking ass in an hour. It took like 3 weeks to learn how to actually be effective in my first full fidelity module, the F-16C, but the FC planes can be learned pretty quick, maybe a day or two to be able to fight some AI and some players. Using the mission editor, I've spent most of time creating missions of various realistic and unrealistic scenarios and playing them, or in multiplayer servers constantly dying. But when it all goes right, there is not a more rewarding feeling.
Has a learning curve like a cliff face, but worth every minute.

The good: very detailed combat flight sim. If you like flying then you can easily spend hundreds of hours here.

The bad: While the core is free the modules cost. Each individual one. There are some free 3rd party mods out there but usually lack in polish or function. Still worth checking out. Usually need a paid mod in order to work.

The real bad: Outdated training. Good luck trying to learn with the in house training. You're better off searching google/youtube for how to's. Since each individual mod requires to be paid for there should really be much better and updated training missions/campaigns.

Still a lot of fun, but be prepared for hours of frustration first.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that in-game training modules are outdated, leading players to rely on external sources like YouTube and Google to learn how to operate aircraft.
